title: Operator CR status drift after Helm chart upgrade causing on-prem customer outages
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Several on-prem customers reported pods in their Redwood operator namespace stuck in a transitional state after applying the operator Helm chart 2.7.0 upgrade. The operator CRs show status.conditions array truncated to an empty list and controller reconcile loops never mark resources as Ready. This ticket drives a safe hotfix, a targeted remediation runbook for affected clusters, and follow-up automation to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Install operator helm chart v2.6.x on a k8s 1.26 cluster
2) Upgrade to helm chart v2.7.0 with default values (no custom finalizers)
3) Observe operator logs: frequent leader-election requeue messages and intermittent API timeouts
4) kubectl get <CustomResource> -n redwood shows status.conditions == [] and lastTransitionTime unchanged
5) Some nodeagent DaemonSet pods restart repeatedly and remain NotReady
investigation_summary: Initial triage: Customer support escalated multiple clusters within a 6 hour window showing identical symptoms.
Logs from affected clusters indicate a spike in apiserver latency (~500-800ms) coincident with Helm post-upgrade hooks running.

Operator reconciliation loop attempted to patch CR status while a post-upgrade hook mutated a dependent ConfigMap, causing a resourceVersion conflict and a partial write that left the status array empty.

Helm chart change: reorder of finalizer + new post-upgrade migration job introduced in 2.7.0 that uses kubectl client inside a Job. The job set status.waitForCompletion = true which increased API pressure on small customer control planes.
Reproduction in staging with simulated apiserver latency reproduced truncated status.conditions in ~40% of trials.
A temporary kubectl patch (kubectl patch <CR> --type=json ...) restores conditions and unblocks the operator reconcile.
No data loss observed; primary impact is availability while the CRs are stuck and dependent workloads are not transitioned.
root_cause: A change in helm chart 2.7.0 introduced a synchronous migration job and reordered finalizer handling which, when combined with transient apiserver latency on low-resource customer clusters, caused concurrent writes and partial status updates leaving CR status arrays empty and preventing operator progress.
temporary_mitigations: 1) Instruct affected customers to run provided kubectl patch script (one-liner) to restore CR.status.conditions and trigger reconcile.
2) Disable the post-upgrade migration Job for clusters where apiserver latency is high by setting values.migration.enabled=false prior to upgrade.
3) Apply a short-lived webhook admission delay (increase leader-election lease) via helm overrides to reduce churn during upgrades.
4) Engage SRE to raise API server resource requests on high-risk customers where possible (guided recommendation).
5) We rolled out operator image operator:2.7.1-hotfix to two canary customers with a tolerant status-write path that retries on conflict and validates partial updates before persisting.
final_fix_description: Ship operator-2.7.1: add defensive status writes with read-modify-write and strong conflict retries, validate status.conditions length before replacing, and make the migration Job asynchronous (fork-and-forget with status recorded to a ConfigMap) to avoid synchronous apiserver pressure. Update Helm chart to keep finalizer ordering consistent with pre-2.7 semantics and add an opt-in flag for migration jobs. Include an automated pre-upgrade check that fails fast when apiserver latencies exceed safe thresholds.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish hotfix operator-2.7.1 image and chart with migration.enabled=false by default
2) Canary rollout to two affected customers (small clusters) with 48h monitoring window
3) If canary passes, push a staggered upgrade schedule for remaining affected customers with support coordination
4) For self-managed customers: provide patch manifest and automated script to apply 2.7.1 with minimal downtime
5) Add health checks to Console to detect post-upgrade CR status drift and surface customers in the upgrade dashboard
postmortem_followups: Create an automated pre-upgrade apiserver-latency check and surface in the upgrade CLI
Add an integration test that simulates API timeouts during helm hook execution in CI
Document recommended helm override set for air-gapped / low-resource clusters
Ship a drift-detection controller that alerts when CR.status is cleared unexpectedly
Update runbooks and support templates with the kubectl patch remediation and customer communication scripts
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/191 - chart: make migration job async + finalizer reorder revert
notes: Customer comms drafted and approved by PM; first outbound batch scheduled after canary confirms stability.
SRE monitored API server p99 latency; alert thresholds temporarily lowered for the rollout window.
Security review: migration job runs kubectl in-cluster; we removed cluster-admin ops and limited RBAC scope in 2.7.1 (security_review_required=true).
Next update planned: 2026-03-18 status check and close if no regressions observed for 7 days post-rollout.
